newsitem.title: RUSSIA: US-powered Russian cargo plane makes maiden flight.
newsitem.headline: US-powered Russian cargo plane makes maiden flight.

text.p: A Russian Ilyushin Il-96T cargo aircraft powered by American engines and controlled by American avionics made its maiden test flight in southern Russia on Friday.

The $70-million wide-body freighter, with engines from Pratt and Whitney, and parts from 10 other U.S. firms, took off from Voronezh, 550 km (340 miles) south of Moscow and flew for 21 minutes, an Aeroflot airline spokesman said.
Alexander Luchaninov told Reuters by telephone from Voronezh that Aeroflot hoped to have the plane operating on regular cargo routes this September.
The aircraft, which can carry 50 tonnes over 11,000 km (6,875 miles) or 92 tonnes over 5,000 km (3,125 miles), was rolled out in April, several months late due to funding problems.
"We believe that such planes will help us to make the passenger and cargo service safer and more profitable," Luchaninov said.

Aeroflot, the sole customer of the aircraft so far, ordered 20 of the Pratt and Whitney-powered Il-96s, in both cargo and passenger versions, for delivery by 2001 in a deal worth $1.5 billion funded by the U.S. Eximbank and European and Russian banks with financial guarantees from the Russian government.
Luchaninov said that two other freighters would be delivered in 1998 as well as the first passenger version known as Il-96M.
Last month, Pratt and Whitney officials said the new jet may be certified in Russia and in the United States and could also be marketed outside Russia.
Luchaninov said the Il-96T wiould be desplayed at the Paris Air Show in June. "The plane will make a few demonstration flights at Le Bourget," he said.
